newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexicans bringing AIDS back home from U.S..
newsitem.headline: Mexicans bringing AIDS back home from U.S..

text.p: Mexican immigrants are catching AIDS in the United States and spreading the disease in their rural hometowns when they return to visit, Health Minister Juan Ramon de la Fuente said on Monday.
Compounding the problem, few Mexicans were being honest about the disease when they tested HIV-positive, preferring to hide their condition, he added.

"AIDS is beginning to have a rural profile in some regions, which is worrying," de la Fuente told foreign correspondents. "It is not through blood transfusions or intravenous drug use; it is through heterosexual contact."
Mexican migrant workers "are infected in the United States and when they return to the country they start disseminating AIDS," he said. "The majority of them don't know they are ill."
The problem was particularly acute in states with high migration to the United States such as Zacatecas, Baja California and parts of Jalisco, he added.

Preliminary Health Ministry figures showed that 4,216 cases of full-blown AIDS were reported last year, a broadly similar number to 1995. Around 30,000 AIDS cases have been recorded in Mexico since the first reported instance of the disease in 1986.
But de la Fuente said one-third of last year's AIDS cases were reported from death certificates, indicating the number was almost certainly higher.
Around 140,000 Mexicans were probably HIV-positive but had either hidden the fact or did not yet realise, he estimated.
"Mexican society has still not shaken off the stigma" surrounding AIDS or gotten over the mistaken idea that the disease is something that affects only homosexuals and drug users, de la Fuente said.

Mexico's main health efforts this year will be directed toward decentralizing health care to the states and implementing a World Bank-backed programme to spread basic health care to the estimated 10 million poor Mexicans who currently lack it, he concluded.
